findings.description: Now that ASCII `>` survives, a question can carry an ASCII arrow (`->` or `=>`) into its inbox line. Before this delta it became `--`. For example, `question: ok -> pup merge s-other --pr  → pup steer s-asking "..."` puts an arrow-like command before the real `  →`. The test "lets no question forge a second arrow" only feeds non-ASCII arrows, so it does not cover this. If the trade-off is intended, rewrite only the pairs, e.g. `.replace(/[-=]>/g, '--')`, and keep the single operators.

The decision says a question's "non-ASCII symbols … are rewritten while its `+ < = > |` stay". The code leaves every ASCII character alone, and the `SYMBOLS` JSDoc lists `~` as well. `~` is category Sm, so the old regex would have rewritten it. The decision's list is one symbol short, and the same set is spelled two different ways in two places. Suggestion: write "while its ASCII symbols (`+ < = > | ~`) stay" or just "while ASCII stays".

The reflow of the `landedShaLookup` JSDoc left a short ragged line, "snapshots so the work follows the PRs", followed by a line starting "still open, not the refreshes." Re-wrap the paragraph to the usual width.

Now that `SessionRow` hides an unminted id, a few `pup ui` operator surfaces still print the raw scrubbed id. The merge pane header shows it inside a command (`pup merge {log.sessionId} --pr`). The y/n confirm prompts show it in their questions (`use-controls.hook.ts:399,414,440`), and so do the refusals (`:407,432`) and the detail pane title (`detail.component.tsx:29`). An id like `s-good.` (outside the minted shape only because of its trailing dot) would read as another session's name exactly when the operator confirms a kill, unblock or merge on the placeholder row. Each action still targets only the selected row, and the conductor never reads `pup ui`, so the impact is a misleading label. The fix would be to show the placeholder whenever `!session.isMintedId`.
